main_body: Stone forge: a chimney hood on top and a firebox with fire and a stone hearth below, all seen face-on
top_band: Rows 1-3 light grey (L=137) inside a dark outline, then a 1-row light line at row 5. This reads as the chimney-hood face, not a surface seen from above. Rows 7-16 below it are the same grey as the front (L~103).
evidence: The column scan shows a thin grey cap (rows 1-3) and a bright 1-row line at row 5, with no clear horizontal top surface. Below that the stack, firebox, flames and hearth are all vertical faces painted flat. The fire opening is a face-on black slot with flames, so no inside surface is seen from above. The light bar at row 25 is a thin hearth lip. There is no roof or lintel top slope, so this is a front elevation with a hat band.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 16 distinct colours against 185 and 66 for the references. The grey stone has about 4 steps with a checker pattern, and the fire has a good ramp. 81% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7-9% for the references, so the outline is the near-black sticker look rather than a dark tone of the neighbouring material. The stones are not shaded one by one as in the references, and the many sparse, uniform grey blocks read as simple. Colours per tile (15) are comparable, but overall craft is thinner than the references.
